questions.q: Which of the following is considered an 'overhead cost' that must be appropriately factored into the general pricing structure for mobile phone repairs?
options: The direct wholesale cost of an OLED replacement screen for a specific client.
The specific cost of an earpiece speaker requested by a single customer.
Monthly commercial shop rent and utility electricity bills.
The transportation fee paid to a courier to deliver one specific phone to a customer.
questions.explain: Overhead costs represent ongoing business expenses not directly attributable to any single specific repair job—such as rent, basic electricity, and standard administrative software. These must be spread across all repairs to ensure actual profitability.

questions.q: A technician replaces a smartphone charging flex. The wholesale part costs $5.00, courier shipping is $2.00, and the actual repair takes 30 minutes. If the business values technician labor at $40.00/hour and dictates a strict 20% profit markup strictly on parts and shipping costs, what is the precise final repair quote for the customer?
questions.explain: Combined cost of parts & shipping = $5.00 + $2.00 = $7.00. Adding a 20% markup on $7.00 ($7.00 x 0.20) = $1.40 markup. Total part charge to customer = $8.40. For labor, 30 minutes at an hourly rate of $40.00 = $20.00. Total final quote = $20.00 labor + $8.40 parts = $28.40.

questions.q: A GSM laboratory operates an ultrasonic cleaner needing highly specialized deoxidizing chemical fluid that degrades and must be entirely replaced after every 20 motherboard washes. If a single gallon of this fluid costs $50.00, what is the most accurate accounting method to recover this operational cost when pricing a customer's liquid-damage repair?
options: Financially punish the unlucky 20th customer by applying a sudden $50.00 surcharge to their final bill.
Write off the chemical fluid as unrecoverable shop waste and simply charge standard diagnostic labor rates.
Incorporate a mathematically calculated $2.50 consumable overhead surcharge specifically into every single water-damage estimate.
Deduct the total $50.00 fluid cost directly from the junior technician's weekly payroll.
questions.explain: $50.00 divided by 20 uses equates to precisely $2.50. This direct 'consumable' cost is structurally necessary for the repair and must be systematically rolled into the base cost of every water-damage quote to sustain true business profitability.

questions.q: A specialized mobile technician determines a labor cost of exactly $50.00 and logs a core replacement motherboard IC part cost of $30.00. To structurally offset aggressive building lease overheads and utilities, the shop accounting software injects a mandated baseline 15% aggregate surcharge applied against the entire raw repair total. What is the absolute final invoice figure charged to the client?
questions.explain: Calculated raw base cost = Labor ($50.00) + Part ($30.00) = $80.00. The established 15% structural overhead surcharge applied directly to $80.00 calculates as (0.15 x 80 = $12.00). Final cumulative invoice total = $80.00 + $12.00 = $92.00 flat.
